Review: The experiment is feasible in principle if the 111-unit array can independently vary coupling and reliably record synchronized actuator, imaging, and unit-level signals. Its main causal comparison is appropriately prioritized, and the design handles repeated measurements, censoring, and analytic flexibility thoughtfully. The supplied aggregate export motivates the measurements but cannot establish whether the required instrumentation, stable coupling range, or experimental throughput are available. Those uncertainties make feasibility conditional rather than assured.

Feedback: Before committing to the full study, verify that coupling can be changed without materially affecting drive delivery or disorder, and that the chosen settings produce stable, distinct coarsening rates. Use the pilot to assess signal quality, synchronization, run-to-run variability, and the achievable number of independent runs; then set a realistic precision target and observation duration. Specify how initial states will be standardized and how phase-randomized null signals will preserve relevant signal properties. Treat the drive-only and optional disorder conditions as staged extensions, since they add substantial apparatus time and analysis burden. If coupling also changes other physical properties, the causal interpretation should be limited to the effect of the coupling intervention, not attributed specifically to coarsening.

Rating (1-5): 3.
